title: ESA WorldCover 10 m Land Cover (2020 v100, 2021 v200)
description: Global 10 m land-cover maps for the reference years 2020 (algorithm v100) and 2021 (algorithm v200) derived from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, with 11 classes aligned with the UN-FAO Land Cover Classification System. Each 3° × 3° tile also has an InputQuality layer describing the Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 observations used.
purpose: Provides a detailed baseline of land cover across Algeria, including cropland, built-up areas, bare/sparse vegetation, shrubland and water, useful as a stratification or mask for agricultural, ecological and hydrological work.
creator: WorldCover consortium led by VITO Remote Sensing with Brockmann Consult, CS SI (2020 only), Gamma Remote Sensing AG, IIASA and Wageningen University

spatial_extent.description: All land areas observed by Sentinel-2 in 2020 or 2021 except Antarctica, limited to 82.75°N in the north; 2651 tiles of 3° × 3°. Users must select the tiles covering Algeria and clip the country themselves (the viewer also offers download by administrative area).

temporal_extent.description: Two separate single-year maps: 2020 (v100) and 2021 (v200), each representing 1 January–31 December of its reference year. They were produced with different algorithm versions.

variables.name: Map
variables.description: 11 classes: 10 Tree cover, 20 Shrubland, 30 Grassland, 40 Cropland, 50 Built-up, 60 Bare/sparse vegetation, 70 Snow and ice, 80 Permanent water bodies, 90 Herbaceous wetland, 95 Mangroves, 100 Moss and lichen.

variables.name: InputQuality
variables.description: Band 1: number of Sentinel-1 GAMMA0 observations; Band 2: number of Sentinel-2 L2A observations; Band 3: percentage (0–100) of invalid Sentinel-2 observations discarded.

processing: Sentinel-2 L2A observations were cloud-masked using the scene classification layer, aggregated into 10-day median composites and gap-filled by linear interpolation; percentile and other temporal features were computed for Sentinel-2 bands, vegetation indices and Sentinel-1 VV/VH backscatter. A machine-learning classifier trained on reference locations (259,734 locations and 131 features for v100; 319,415 locations and 115 features for v200) predicted class labels and probabilities, after which expert rules using auxiliary datasets were applied and results tiled into 3° × 3° tiles in EPSG:4326.
validation: WorldCover Product Validation Report v2.0: global overall accuracy of the 2021 v200 map 76.7 ± 0.5% (2.16 million secondary sample units at 21,624 primary sample locations). WorldCover Product Validation Report v1.1: global overall accuracy of the 2020 v100 map 74.4 ± 0.1%. Both reports state that the cropland class was mapped with higher accuracy on all continents except Africa, where cropland tended to be under-represented (v100 report: mostly confused with grassland).
limitations: The 2020 and 2021 maps were produced with different algorithm versions; the provider states that most differences between them are due to algorithm changes, so they must not be used directly for change detection.

The Cropland class covers annual crops only; perennial woody crops are classified as tree cover or shrubland (the Tree cover definition explicitly includes olive trees and oil palm), and greenhouses are classified as built-up.
The Grassland class may contain uncultivated cropland (no harvest / bare-soil period) in the reference year, so fallow fields can fall outside the Cropland class.
Known artefacts listed in the PUM include hard borders between Sentinel-2 orbits/blocks in areas of high class confusion and confusion between (irrigated) agriculture and herbaceous wetland.
Cropland accuracy in Africa is reported to be lower (omission) than on other continents.

algeria_notes: Olive groves and date-palm plantations are mapped as tree cover or shrubland, and fallow parcels in the cereal rotation can appear as grassland or bare/sparse vegetation, so WorldCover 'Cropland' will understate total agricultural land in Algeria compared with definitions that include perennial crops and fallow. Most of the Saharan territory falls in the Bare/sparse vegetation class, for which the validation report notes high accuracy in Africa; irrigated centre-pivot fields and oases form small cropland or tree-cover patches within it.
